This applies regardless of task simplicity. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions waste the most time. Exception: `--fast` mode skips research but still requires a plan step. User override: If user explicitly says "just code it" or "skip planning", respect their instruction. Before planning OR asking clarifying questions, scan the codebase. Mandatory scout outputs: 1. Project type, language(s), framework(s) 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the task 3. Current patterns/conventions for similar features (so the implementation matches them) 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any in-flight plans in `./plans/` covering this area 5. Public APIs, schemas, contracts that the task could affect State a 3-6 bullet codebase-context summary to the user before asking questions. Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path (the plan already encodes scout output). Before producing a plan, you MUST be able to answer ALL of these in one concrete sentence each (use `AskUserQuestion` to pin them down — do NOT proceed on vague intent): 1. **Expected output**: the concrete artifact(s) the user will see at the end (file paths, feature behavior, UI screen, API endpoint + payload, CLI command + flags). 2. **Acceptance criteria**: specific behaviors / inputs → outputs / edge cases that MUST work to call it "done". 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope this round. 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines, performance. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will be modified or extended; which contracts must stay stable. Ground every `AskUserQuestion` option in scout findings (e.g., "Add to `src/api/users.ts` (matches existing pattern) or new `src/api/profile.ts`?"). Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path. Implementation is NOT done until verified to be side-effect-free. Code-review and test gates MUST prove: 1. New behavior matches every acceptance criterion above. 2. All tests pass — including tests in modules that share files/contracts with the change. 3. No existing business logic / workflow regression: explicitly walk each touchpoint and any caller of changed functions. 4. No new lint/type/build errors anywhere in the repo. 5. Public contracts unchanged unless intentional and called out (function signatures, exported types, API responses, DB schemas, env vars, config keys). User override: If user invoked `--no-test`, item 2 is downgraded to a warning. Surface the unverified-tests risk in the finalize `AskUserQuestion` so the user accepts the trade-off rather than having it silently chosen. Items 1, 3, 4, 5 remain enforceable via the mandatory `code-reviewer` subagent. If review/testing reveals a side effect, regression, or broken workflow, STOP. Use `AskUserQuestion` to present: - What broke (file, test, workflow, user-facing behavior) - Why this implementation caused it (1-line cause) - 2-4 concrete options for the user to choose, e.g.: - "Revert this slice and re-plan with stricter scope" - "Keep the implementation and update to match the new contract" - "Add a compatibility shim at so old callers keep working" - "Accept the regression — old behavior was unintended/buggy" Let the user decide. Do not silently patch around regressions. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to plan" | Simple tasks have hidden complexity. Plan takes 30 seconds. | | "I already know how to do this" | Knowing ≠ planning. Write it down. | | "Let me just start coding" | Undisciplined action wastes tokens. Plan first. | | "The user wants speed" | Fastest path = plan → implement → done. Not: implement → debug → rewrite. | | "I'll plan as I go" | That's not planning, that's hoping. | | "Just this once" | Every skip is "just this once." No exceptions. | ## Smart Intent Detection | Input Pattern | Detected Mode | Behavior | |---------------|---------------|----------| | Path to `plan.md` or `phase-*.md` | code | Execute existing plan | | Contains "fast", "quick" | fast | Skip research, scout→plan→code | | Contains "trust me", "auto" | auto | Auto-approve all steps | | Lists 3+ features OR "parallel" | parallel | Multi-agent execution | | Contains "no test", "skip test" | no-test | Skip testing step | | Default | interactive | Full workflow with user input | See `references/intent-detection.md` for detection logic. ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Intent Detection] --> B{Has plan path?} B -->|Yes| F[Load Plan] B -->|No| C{Mode?} C -->|fast| D[Scout → Plan → Code] C -->|interactive/auto| SC[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] SC --> SR[Summarize Findings to User] SR --> RQ{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} RQ -->|No| SR RQ -->|Yes| E[Research → Review → Plan] E --> F D --> F F --> G[Review Gate] G -->|approved| H[Implement] G -->|rejected| E H --> H1{Simplify signal?} H1 -->|Yes| H2[Conditional Simplify] H1 -->|No| I[Review Gate] H2 --> I I -->|approved| J{--no-test?} J -->|No| K[Test] J -->|Yes| L[Finalize] K --> L L --> M[Report + Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. ## Workflow Overview ``` [Intent Detection] → [Research?] → [Review] → [Plan] → [Review] → [Implement] → [Conditional Simplify?] → [Review] → [Test?] → [Review] → [Finalize] ``` **Default (non-auto):** Stops at `[Review]` gates for human approval before each major step. **Auto mode (`--auto`):** Skips human review gates, implements all phases continuously. **Claude Tasks:** Utilize `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList` during implementation step. **Fallback:** These are CLI-only tools — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for progress tracking instead. | Mode | Research | Testing | Review Gates | Phase Progression | |------|----------|---------|--------------|-------------------| | interactive | ✓ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | auto | ✓ | ✓ | Auto if score≥9.5 | All at once (no stops) | | fast | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | parallel | Optional | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Parallel groups | | no-test | ✓ | ✗ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | code | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Per plan | ## Step Output Format ``` ✓ Step [N]: [Brief status] - [Key metrics] ``` ## Blocking Gates (Non-Auto Mode) Human review required at these checkpoints (skipped with `--auto`): - **Post-Research:** Review findings before planning - **Post-Plan:** Approve plan before implementation - **Post-Implementation:** Approve code before testing - **Post-Testing:** 100% pass + approve before finalize **Always enforced (all modes):** - **Testing:** 100% pass required (unless no-test mode) - **Code Review (MANDATORY):** Spawn `code-reviewer` subagent with explicit checks: (a) every acceptance criterion met, (b) no regression to business logic in touchpoints/blast-radius, (c) no breaking changes to public contracts (signatures, schemas, APIs, env vars) unless called out, (d) follows existing patterns from scout, (e) no new lint/type/build errors anywhere. Pass scout summary + acceptance criteria as context. If reviewer flags side effects → trigger HARD-GATE-NO-SIDE-EFFECTS (`AskUserQuestion` with 2-4 options). Then: User approval OR auto-approve (score≥9.5, 0 critical). - **Finalize (MANDATORY - never skip):** 1. **Activate `/ck:project-management` skill (MANDATORY)** → run full plan sync-back across ALL `phase-XX-*.md` (not only current phase), update `plan.md` status/progress, hydrate Claude Tasks, generate progress report 2. `docs-manager` subagent → update `./docs` if changes warrant 3. `TaskUpdate` → mark all Claude Tasks complete after sync-back verification (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Ask user if they want to commit via `git-manager` subagent 5. Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ## Required Subagents (MANDATORY) | Phase | Subagent | Requirement | |-------|----------|-------------| | Research | `researcher` | Optional in fast/code | | Scout | `ck:scout` | Optional in code | | Plan | `planner` | Optional in code | | UI Work | `ui-ux-designer` | If frontend work | | Testing | `tester`, `debugger` | **MUST** spawn | | Review | `code-reviewer` | **MUST** spawn | | Finalize | `/ck:project-management` skill + `docs-manager`, `git-manager` subagents | **MUST** invoke all | **CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT:** - Steps 4, 5, 6 **MUST** use Task tool to spawn subagents - DO NOT implement testing, review, or finalization yourself - DELEGATE - If workflow ends with 0 Task tool calls, it is INCOMPLETE - Pattern: `Task(subagent_type="[type]", prompt="[task]", description="[brief]")` ## References - `references/intent-detection.md` - Detection rules and routing logic - `references/workflow-steps.md` - Detailed step definitions for all modes - `references/review-cycle.md` - Interactive and auto review processes - `references/subagent-patterns.md` - Subagent invocation patterns ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:plan` (execute a plan), `/ck:brainstorm` (implement agreed solution) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:code-review` (review after implementation), `/ck:test` (validate changes) **Related:** `/ck:fix` (alternative for bug fixes), `/ck:plan` (create plan before cooking) ARGUMENTS: plans/260608-codeflow-gap-closure-tdd/plan.md

## Code Review Summary

### Scope
- Files: `provenance.rs`, `budget_policy.rs`, `router.rs`, `budget_cmd.rs`
- LOC: ~750 across 4 files (new + existing)
- Focus: Phase 1 CODEFLOW gap closure

### Overall Assessment
Clean, well-structured implementation. All acceptance criteria met. Backward compatibility preserved. No security issues found.

### Acceptance Criteria Verification

1. **model_id extraction**: `extract_model_id()` checks `CLAUDE_MODEL` env first, then hook JSON `model` field, falls back to `"unknown"`. Correct precedence. PASS.
2. **6-field attestation signature**: Line 400-403 signs `prompt_hash:model_id:model_version:code_hash:timestamp:developer_id`. Test at line 706-712 verifies round-trip. PASS.
3. **Line-level blame via diff**: `parse_diff_ranges()` parses `@@ +c,d @@` format, falls back to `1..line_count` when no git diff available (line 391-397). PASS.
4. **Team scope in budget**: `evaluate_with_team()` handles `"team"` scope with wildcard/specific matching, env var fallback via `CODEFLOW_TEAM`. No team = rule skipped. PASS.
5. **Router downgrades on budget pressure**: `classify_with_budget()` downgrades Opus to Sonnet on Warn, forces Haiku on Block. Non-Opus tiers unaffected by Warn. PASS.
6. **Webhook body format**: Correct JSON with `policy_id`, `action`, `spent_usd`, `limit_usd`, `percentage`. PASS.
7. **Backward compat**: `detect_changes()` delegates to `detect_changes_with_model(..., None)`. Caller in `main.rs:410` still calls old signature. `evaluate()` delegates to `evaluate_with_team(..., None, 0.0)`. PASS.

### Issues Found

**Medium** — `extract_model_id` tests (lines 651-680) use `set_var`/`remove_var` on `CLAUDE_MODEL`. These are **not thread-safe** in Rust's parallel test runner. If another test reads `CLAUDE_MODEL` concurrently, results are nondeterministic. Recommend `#[serial]` from `serial_test` crate, or consolidate env-dependent tests into one `#[test]`.

**Low** — `dispatch_webhook()` (line 191-196) silently discards HTTP errors via `let _ =`. Acceptable for fire-and-forget alerts, but caller has no way to know if delivery failed. Consider returning `Result` or logging on failure.

**Low** — `status()` function (line 71) does not account for `"team"` scope when displaying accumulated cost (defaults to `0.0`). The display table will show team rules at $0.00 spent even when team data exists.

### Positive Observations
- TDD structure visible: "Step A: Lock existing" then "Step B: New behavior" pattern in tests.
- `parse_diff_ranges` correctly handles the `count=0` case (pure deletions produce no range).
- Budget engine's `max_usd == 0.0` edge case handled (returns 100%).
- Signature test does actual cryptographic verification round-trip, not just "is non-empty".

### Recommended Actions
1. Fix env var test thread-safety (medium).
2. Optional: surface webhook dispatch errors or log them.
3. Optional: add team accumulated cost to `status()` display.

# Phase 1: Fix Foundations

## Overview

Fix 6 partial implementations in existing CLI code. model_id extraction, full attestation envelope, line-level blame, team budget scope, router-budget integration, push alerts.

## Requirements

- Functional: model_id extracted from hook context, attestation signs all 6 fields, blame shows line ranges not whole-file, budget supports team scope, router checks budget before suggesting tier, webhook alerts on threshold
- Non-functional: all existing tests pass, <5ms overhead per hook call

## Architecture

```
Hook JSON → extract model_id → provenance.rs → detect_changes() with git diff lines
                                     ↓
                              sign full envelope (6 fields)
                                     ↓
                              blame shows per-line ranges
                                     
Budget TOML → team scope → PolicyEngine.evaluate() → Verdict
                                     ↓
                              router.rs consults budget → downgrade tier
                                     ↓
                              webhook POST on warn/block
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `cli/crates/core/src/provenance.rs` — model_id, line ranges, envelope
- Modify: `cli/crates/core/src/session.rs` — extract model_id from hook JSON
- Modify: `cli/crates/core/src/budget_policy.rs` — add team scope
- Modify: `cli/crates/core/src/router.rs` — add budget consultation
- Modify: `cli/crates/cli/src/hooks.rs` — pass model_id through pipeline
- Modify: `cli/crates/cli/src/budget_cmd.rs` — webhook alert dispatch

## Implementation Steps

### TDD Step A: Write tests for current behavior (lock regressions)

1. Add test `test_detect_changes_preserves_existing_fields` in provenance.rs — verify session_id, file_path, code_hash, contributor_type, attestation_sig are all populated after detect_changes()
2. Add test `test_budget_evaluate_developer_scope` — verify existing dev scope Allow/Warn/Block verdicts
3. Add test `test_budget_evaluate_project_scope` — verify existing project scope verdicts
4. Add test `test_router_classify_complexity_levels` — verify Low/Medium/High classification unchanged
5. Add test `test_blame_output_format` — verify blame produces records with expected fields
6. Run `cargo test` — all must pass. This locks current behavior.

### TDD Step B: Write tests for NEW behavior (red tests)

7. Add test `test_model_id_from_env_var` — set `CLAUDE_MODEL=claude-opus-4`, call extraction, expect "claude-opus-4"
8. Add test `test_model_id_from_hook_json` — pass `{"model": "claude-sonnet-4"}` JSON, expect extraction

# Phase 2: Quality Gate — codeflow gate + dep validation

Exit: 0=pass, 1=blocked, 2=error

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\cook # Cook - Smart Feature Implementation End-to-end implementation with automatic workflow detection. **Principles:** YAGNI, KISS, DRY | Token efficiency | Concise reports ## Usage ``` /ck:cook ``` **IMPORTANT:** If no flag is provided, the skill will use the `interactive` mode by default for the workflow. **Optional flags to select the workflow mode:** - `--interactive`: Full workflow with user input (**default**) - `--fast`: Skip research, scout→plan→code - `--parallel`: Multi-agent execution - `--no-test`: Skip testing step - `--auto`: Auto-approve all steps **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): - `--tdd`: Tests-first per phase — write tests for current behavior before refactoring, then verify they still pass after the implementation step **Example:** ``` /ck:cook "Add user authentication to the app" --fast /ck:cook path/to/plan.md --auto /ck:cook "Refactor auth middleware" --tdd ``` Do NOT write implementation code until a plan exists and has been reviewed. This applies regardless of task simplicity. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions waste the most time. Exception: `--fast` mode skips research but still requires a plan step. User override: If user explicitly says "just code it" or "skip planning", respect their instruction. Before planning OR asking clarifying questions, scan the codebase. Mandatory scout outputs: 1. Project type, language(s), framework(s) 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the task 3. Current patterns/conventions for similar features (so the implementation matches them) 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any in-flight plans in `./plans/` covering this area 5. Public APIs, schemas, contracts that the task could affect State a 3-6 bullet codebase-context summary to the user before asking questions. Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path (the plan already encodes scout output). Before producing a plan, you MUST be able to answer ALL of these in one concrete sentence each (use `AskUserQuestion` to pin them down — do NOT proceed on vague intent): 1. **Expected output**: the concrete artifact(s) the user will see at the end (file paths, feature behavior, UI screen, API endpoint + payload, CLI command + flags). 2. **Acceptance criteria**: specific behaviors / inputs → outputs / edge cases that MUST work to call it "done". 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope this round. 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines, performance. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will be modified or extended; which contracts must stay stable. Ground every `AskUserQuestion` option in scout findings (e.g., "Add to `src/api/users.ts` (matches existing pattern) or new `src/api/profile.ts`?"). Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path. Implementation is NOT done until verified to be side-effect-free. Code-review and test gates MUST prove: 1. New behavior matches every acceptance criterion above. 2. All tests pass — including tests in modules that share files/contracts with the change. 3. No existing business logic / workflow regression: explicitly walk each touchpoint and any caller of changed functions. 4. No new lint/type/build errors anywhere in the repo. 5. Public contracts unchanged unless intentional and called out (function signatures, exported types, API responses, DB schemas, env vars, config keys). User override: If user invoked `--no-test`, item 2 is downgraded to a warning. Surface the unverified-tests risk in the finalize `AskUserQuestion` so the user accepts the trade-off rather than having it silently chosen. Items 1, 3, 4, 5 remain enforceable via the mandatory `code-reviewer` subagent. If review/testing reveals a side effect, regression, or broken workflow, STOP. Use `AskUserQuestion` to present: - What broke (file, test, workflow, user-facing behavior) - Why this implementation caused it (1-line cause) - 2-4 concrete options for the user to choose, e.g.: - "Revert this slice and re-plan with stricter scope" - "Keep the implementation and update to match the new contract" - "Add a compatibility shim at so old callers keep working" - "Accept the regression — old behavior was unintended/buggy" Let the user decide. Do not silently patch around regressions. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to plan" | Simple tasks have hidden complexity. Plan takes 30 seconds. | | "I already know how to do this" | Knowing ≠ planning. Write it down. | | "Let me just start coding" | Undisciplined action wastes tokens. Plan first. | | "The user wants speed" | Fastest path = plan → implement → done. Not: implement → debug → rewrite. | | "I'll plan as I go" | That's not planning, that's hoping. | | "Just this once" | Every skip is "just this once." No exceptions. | ## Smart Intent Detection | Input Pattern | Detected Mode | Behavior | |---------------|---------------|----------| | Path to `plan.md` or `phase-*.md` | code | Execute existing plan | | Contains "fast", "quick" | fast | Skip research, scout→plan→code | | Contains "trust me", "auto" | auto | Auto-approve all steps | | Lists 3+ features OR "parallel" | parallel | Multi-agent execution | | Contains "no test", "skip test" | no-test | Skip testing step | | Default | interactive | Full workflow with user input | See `references/intent-detection.md` for detection logic. ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Intent Detection] --> B{Has plan path?} B -->|Yes| F[Load Plan] B -->|No| C{Mode?} C -->|fast| D[Scout → Plan → Code] C -->|interactive/auto| SC[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] SC --> SR[Summarize Findings to User] SR --> RQ{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} RQ -->|No| SR RQ -->|Yes| E[Research → Review → Plan] E --> F D --> F F --> G[Review Gate] G -->|approved| H[Implement] G -->|rejected| E H --> H1{Simplify signal?} H1 -->|Yes| H2[Conditional Simplify] H1 -->|No| I[Review Gate] H2 --> I I -->|approved| J{--no-test?} J -->|No| K[Test] J -->|Yes| L[Finalize] K --> L L --> M[Report + Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. ## Workflow Overview ``` [Intent Detection] → [Research?] → [Review] → [Plan] → [Review] → [Implement] → [Conditional Simplify?] → [Review] → [Test?] → [Review] → [Finalize] ``` **Default (non-auto):** Stops at `[Review]` gates for human approval before each major step. **Auto mode (`--auto`):** Skips human review gates, implements all phases continuously. **Claude Tasks:** Utilize `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList` during implementation step. **Fallback:** These are CLI-only tools — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for progress tracking instead. | Mode | Research | Testing | Review Gates | Phase Progression | |------|----------|---------|--------------|-------------------| | interactive | ✓ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | auto | ✓ | ✓ | Auto if score≥9.5 | All at once (no stops) | | fast | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | parallel | Optional | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Parallel groups | | no-test | ✓ | ✗ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | code | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Per plan | ## Step Output Format ``` ✓ Step [N]: [Brief status] - [Key metrics] ``` ## Blocking Gates (Non-Auto Mode) Human review required at these checkpoints (skipped with `--auto`): - **Post-Research:** Review findings before planning - **Post-Plan:** Approve plan before implementation - **Post-Implementation:** Approve code before testing - **Post-Testing:** 100% pass + approve before finalize **Always enforced (all modes):** - **Testing:** 100% pass required (unless no-test mode) - **Code Review (MANDATORY):** Spawn `code-reviewer` subagent with explicit checks: (a) every acceptance criterion met, (b) no regression to business logic in touchpoints/blast-radius, (c) no breaking changes to public contracts (signatures, schemas, APIs, env vars) unless called out, (d) follows existing patterns from scout, (e) no new lint/type/build errors anywhere. Pass scout summary + acceptance criteria as context. If reviewer flags side effects → trigger HARD-GATE-NO-SIDE-EFFECTS (`AskUserQuestion` with 2-4 options). Then: User approval OR auto-approve (score≥9.5, 0 critical). - **Finalize (MANDATORY - never skip):** 1. **Activate `/ck:project-management` skill (MANDATORY)** → run full plan sync-back across ALL `phase-XX-*.md` (not only current phase), update `plan.md` status/progress, hydrate Claude Tasks, generate progress report 2. `docs-manager` subagent → update `./docs` if changes warrant 3. `TaskUpdate` → mark all Claude Tasks complete after sync-back verification (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Ask user if they want to commit via `git-manager` subagent 5. Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ## Required Subagents (MANDATORY) | Phase | Subagent | Requirement | |-------|----------|-------------| | Research | `researcher` | Optional in fast/code | | Scout | `ck:scout` | Optional in code | | Plan | `planner` | Optional in code | | UI Work | `ui-ux-designer` | If frontend work | | Testing | `tester`, `debugger` | **MUST** spawn | | Review | `code-reviewer` | **MUST** spawn | | Finalize | `/ck:project-management` skill + `docs-manager`, `git-manager` subagents | **MUST** invoke all | **CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT:** - Steps 4, 5, 6 **MUST** use Task tool to spawn subagents - DO NOT implement testing, review, or finalization yourself - DELEGATE - If workflow ends with 0 Task tool calls, it is INCOMPLETE - Pattern: `Task(subagent_type="[type]", prompt="[task]", description="[brief]")` ## References - `references/intent-detection.md` - Detection rules and routing logic - `references/workflow-steps.md` - Detailed step definitions for all modes - `references/review-cycle.md` - Interactive and auto review processes - `references/subagent-patterns.md` - Subagent invocation patterns ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:plan` (execute a plan), `/ck:brainstorm` (implement agreed solution) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:code-review` (review after implementation), `/ck:test` (validate changes) **Related:** `/ck:fix` (alternative for bug fixes), `/ck:plan` (create plan before cooking) ARGUMENTS: plans/260608-codeflow-gap-closure-tdd/plan.md

**TDD approach:** Each phase writes tests BEFORE implementation. Existing tests must stay green throughout.

# Phase 5: Cloud Proto + API Sync

## Overview

Sync cloud Go backend with CLI Rust proto. Add 4 new event types + messages to cloud proto. Update ClickHouse schema. Add 5 new API endpoints for provenance, cost-by-PR, budget, quality, and compliance export.

## Requirements

- Functional: cloud ingests provenance/cost/governance/quality events, new API endpoints return correct data, ClickHouse stores all new event types
- Non-functional: ingest latency <50ms, API response <200ms, `go test ./...` passes

## Architecture

```
CLI (Rust) emits EventBatch with new event types
    ↓ NATS JetStream / HTTP POST /v1/events
Cloud ingest handler deserializes ALL event types (not just compression+dedup)
    ↓
ClickHouse: new tables
  - provenance_events (file_path, model_id, contributor_type, code_hash, ...)
  - cost_events (model_id, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, ...)
  - governance_events (policy_id, action, budget_remaining, ...)
  - quality_events (check_type, severity, finding, blocked, ...)
    ↓
New API endpoints:
  GET /v1/provenance?project=X&range=90d
  GET /v1/cost/by-pr?project=X
  GET /v1/budget/status?project=X
  GET /v1/quality/summary?project=X
  GET /v1/compliance/export?format=slsa&range=90d
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `cloud/proto/events.proto` — sync with CLI proto (add 4 event types + 4 messages)
- Modify: `cloud/proto/events.pb.go` — regenerate from proto
- Modify: `cloud/internal/clickhouse/client.go` — add new tables, new insert methods
- Modify: `cloud/internal/api/handler_events.go` — deserialize new event types in batchToRows
- Create: `cloud/internal/api/handler_provenance.go` — GET /v1/provenance
- Create: `cloud/internal/api/handler_cost.go` — GET /v1/cost/by-pr
- Create: `cloud/internal/api/handler_budget.go` — GET /v1/budget/status
- Create: `cloud/internal/api/handler_quality.go` — GET /v1/quality/summary
- Create: `cloud/internal/api/handler_compliance.go` — GET /v1/compliance/export
- Modify: `cloud/internal/api/router.go` — register new endpoints
- Modify: `cloud/internal/api/storage.go` — add new storage interface methods
- Create: `cloud/cmd/migrate/migrations/002_add_pillar_tables.sql` — ClickHouse DDL

## Implementation Steps

### TDD Step A: Lock existing Go test behavior

1. Run `go test ./...` in cloud/ — capture baseline pass count
2. Read existing `handler_events_test.go` — verify compression+dedup ingest tests pass
3. Read existing `handler_query_test.go` — verify overview/project stats tests pass

### TDD Step B: Write tests for NEW behavior (red)

4. Add `handler_provenance_test.go`:
   - `TestProvenanceQuery_ReturnsRecords` — insert provenance events, GET /v1/provenance → 200 with records
   - `TestProvenanceQuery_FilterByProject` — filter by project_dir
   - `TestProvenanceQuery_FilterByDateRange` — range param
5. Add `handler_cost_test.go`:
   - `TestCostByPR_GroupsByPR` — insert cost events with different pr_ref, GET /v1/cost/by-pr → grouped
   - `TestCostByPR_IncludesModelBreakdown` — each PR group has per-model cost
6. Add `handler_budget_test.go`:
   - `TestBudgetStatus_ReturnsSummary` — GET /v1/budget/status → spend summary
7. Add `handler_quality_test.go`:
   - `TestQualitySummary_CountsFindings` — insert quality events, GET → finding counts by type
   - `TestQualitySummary_PassFailRate` — gate pass/fail percentage
8. Add `handler_compliance_test.go`:
   - `TestComplianceExport_SLSA` — GET /v1/compliance/export?format=slsa → valid SLSA JSON
   - `TestComplianceExport_CycloneDX` — format=cyclonedx → valid CycloneDX JSON
9. Add `handler_events_test.go` extension:
   - `TestIngestProvenanceEvent` — POST event with provenance → stored in ClickHouse
   - `TestIngestCostEvent` — POST event with cost → stored
   - `TestIngestGovernanceEvent` — POST governance event → stored
   - `TestIngestQualityEvent` — POST quality event → stored
10. Run `go test ./...` — new tests FAIL (red)

### TDD Step C: Implement

11. **Sync cloud proto** — Copy `cli/proto/events.proto` content to `cloud/proto/events.proto`. Keep Go package option. Regenerate:
    ```bash
    protoc --go_out=. --go_opt=paths=source_relative cloud/proto/events.proto
    ```
12. **ClickHouse migration** — `002_add_pillar_tables.sql`:
    ```sql
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS provenance_events (
        id UUID DEFAULT generateUUIDv4(),
        timestamp_ms Int64,
        session_id String,
        project_dir String,
        machine_id String,
        file_path String,
        code_hash String,
        model_id String,
        model_version String,
        contributor_type String,
        start_line UInt32,
        end_line UInt32,
        attestation_sig String,
        developer_id String,
        prompt_hash String
    ) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (project_dir, timestamp_ms);

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cost_events ( ... ) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (project_dir, timestamp_ms);
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS governance_events ( ... ) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (project_dir, timestamp_ms);
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS quality_events ( ... ) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (project_dir, timestamp_ms);
    ```
13. **Update storage.go** — Add interface methods:
    ```go
    type Storage interface {
        // existing...
        InsertProvenanceEvents(ctx, []ProvenanceRow) error
        InsertCostEvents(ctx, []CostRow) error
        InsertGovernanceEvents(ctx, []GovernanceRow) error
        InsertQualityEvents(ctx, []QualityRow) error
        QueryProvenance(ctx, project, from, to) ([]ProvenanceRow, error)
        QueryCostByPR(ctx, project) ([]CostByPR, error)
        QueryBudgetStatus(ctx, project) (*BudgetSummary, error)
        QueryQualitySummary(ctx, project) (*QualitySummary, error)
    }
    ```
14. **Update handler_events.go batchToRows** — Add cases for Provenance, Cost, Governance, Quality event types. Currently only handles Compression and Dedup.
15. **handler_provenance.go** — Standard query handler with project + date range filters
16. **handler_cost.go** — Group by pr_ref, sum cost_usd, breakdown by model_id
17. **handler_budget.go** — Aggregate governance events, return latest budget state
18. **handler_quality.go** — Count findings by check_type + severity, calculate pass/fail rate
19. **handler_compliance.go** — Reuse SLSA/CycloneDX generation logic (port from Rust or call CLI)
20. **router.go** — Register 5 new routes

### TDD Step D: Verify

21. Run `go test ./...` — ALL pass
22. Run `go vet ./...` — clean
23. Docker compose up — verify ClickHouse migration runs
24. Manual test: POST event with provenance payload → GET /v1/provenance returns it
25. Manual test: POST cost events → GET /v1/cost/by-pr returns grouped data

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Cloud proto has all 6 event types + 4 messages (synced with CLI)
- [ ] ClickHouse has 4 new tables (provenance, cost, governance, quality)
- [ ] Ingest handler stores all event types (not just compression+dedup)
- [ ] 5 new API endpoints return correct data
- [ ] `go test ./...` all pass
- [ ] Docker compose up + migrate works

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Proto regeneration breaks existing handlers | Run full test suite after regen. Proto is additive-only. |
| ClickHouse schema migration on existing data | New tables only, no ALTER on existing tables. Safe. |
| Compliance export in Go duplicates Rust logic | Phase 1 approach: simple JSON serialization in Go. Shared test fixtures validate output shape matches. |

10	type RouterOption func(*handler)
11	
12	func WithPublisher(p EventPublisher) RouterOption {
13		return func(h *handler) { h.publisher = p }
14	}
15	
16	func NewRouter(store Storage, logger *slog.Logger, opts ...RouterOption) http.Handler {
17		apiMux := http.NewServeMux()
18	
19		h := &handler{store: store, hub: newWSHub(), logger: logger}
20		for _, opt := range opts {
21			opt(h)
22		}
23	
24		apiMux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/events", h.handleIngestEvents)
25		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/overview", h.handleOverview)
26		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/projects", h.handleListProjects)
27		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/projects/{id}/stats", h.handleProjectStats)
28		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/savings/trend", h.handleSavingsTrend)
29		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/waste", h.handleWasteReport)
30		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/waste/projects", h.handleProjectWasteScores)
31		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/security/alerts", h.handleSecurityAlerts)
32		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/billing/status", h.handleBillingStatus)
33		apiMux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/billing/checkout", h.handleCreateCheckout)
34		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/export/csv", h.handleExportCSV)
35		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/roi", h.handleROISummary)
36		apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/ws", h.handleWebSocket)
37	
38		rl := newRateLimiter()
39	
40		var wrapped http.Handler = apiMux
41		wrapped = withRateLimit(rl)(wrapped)
42		wrapped = withTenantAuth(wrapped)
43		wrapped = withCORS(wrapped)
44	
45		root := http.NewServeMux()
46		root.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", h.handleHealthz)
47		root.HandleFunc("POST /v1/billing/webhook", h.handleStripeWebhook)
48		root.Handle("/", wrapped)
49	
50		return withLogging(logger, root)
51	}

53	func (h *handler) handleHealthz(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
54		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
55		defer cancel()
56	
57		if err := h.store.Ping(ctx); err != nil {
58			h.logger.Error("healthz ping failed", "error", err)
59			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
60			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusServiceUnavailable)
61			w.Write([]byte(`{"status":"unhealthy"}`))
62			return
63		}
64	
65		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
66		w.Write([]byte(`{"status":"ok"}`))
67	}
68	
69	func withLogging(logger *slog.Logger, next http.Handler) http.Handler {
70		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
71			logger.Info("request",
72				"method", r.Method,
73				"path", r.URL.Path,
74				"remote", r.RemoteAddr,
75			)
76			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
77		})
78	}

1	package clickhouse
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"time"
8	
9		ch "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
10	)
11	
12	type Client struct {
13		conn ch.Conn
14	}
15	
16	type EventRow struct {
17		EventID          string
18		TenantID         string
19		Timestamp        time.Time
20		SessionID        string
21		ProjectDir       string
22		Command          string
23		EventType        string
24		InputBytes       uint64
25		OutputBytes      uint64
26		InputTokens      uint64
27		OutputTokens     uint64
28		TokensSaved      uint64
29		FilterName       string
30		CompressionLevel string
31		LatencyMs        float64
32		ContentHash      string
33		CacheHit         bool
34		CLIVersion       string
35		MachineID        string
36	}
37	
38	type OverviewStats struct {
39		TotalInputTokens  uint64  `json:"total_input_tokens"`
40		TotalOutputTokens uint64  `json:"total_output_tokens"`
41		TotalSaved        uint64  `json:"total_saved"`
42		SavingsPct        float64 `json:"savings_pct"`
43		EventCount        uint64  `json:"event_count"`
44		TopCommands       []CommandStat `json:"top_commands"`
45	}
46	
47	type CommandStat struct {
48		Command string `json:"command"`
49		Saved   uint64 `json:"saved"`
50		Count   uint64 `json:"count"`
51	}
52	
53	func New(dsn string) (*Client, error) {
54		opts, err := ch.ParseDSN(dsn)
55		if err != nil {
56			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse dsn: %w", err)
57		}
58	
59		conn, err := ch.Open(opts)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open connection: %w", err)
62		}
63	
64		if err := conn.Ping(context.Background()); err != nil {
65			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ping: %w", err)
66		}
67	
68		return &Client{conn: conn}, nil
69	}
70	
71	func (c *Client) Ping(ctx context.Context) error {
72		return c.conn.Ping(ctx)
73	}
74	
75	func (c *Client) Close() error {
76		return c.conn.Close()
77	}
78	
79	func (c *Client) InsertEvents(ctx context.Context, rows []EventRow) error {
80		if len(rows) == 0 {
81			return nil
82		}
83	
84		batch, err := c.conn.PrepareBatch(ctx, `INSERT INTO codeflow.events (
85			event_id, tenant_id, timestamp, session_id, project_dir, command,
86			event_type, input_bytes, output_bytes, input_tokens, output_tokens,
87			tokens_saved, filter_name, compression_level, latency_ms,
88			content_hash, cache_hit, cli_version, machine_id
89		)`)
90		if err != nil {
91			return fmt.Errorf("prepare batch: %w", err)
92		}
93	
94		for _, r := range rows {
95			cacheHitVal := uint8(0)
96			if r.CacheHit {
97				cacheHitVal = 1
98			}
99			if err := batch.Append(
100				r.EventID, r.TenantID, r.Timestamp, r.SessionID, r.ProjectDir, r.Command,
101				r.EventType, r.InputBytes, r.OutputBytes, r.InputTokens, r.OutputTokens,
102				r.TokensSaved, r.FilterName, r.CompressionLevel, r.LatencyMs,
103				r.ContentHash, cacheHitVal, r.CLIVersion, r.MachineID,
104			); err != nil {
105				return fmt.Errorf("append row: %w", err)
106			}
107		}
108	
109		return batch.Send()
110	}
111	
112	func (c *Client) GetOverview(ctx context.Context, tenantID string) (*OverviewStats, error) {
113		var stats OverviewStats
114	
115		row := c.conn.QueryRow(ctx, `
116			SELECT
117				sum(input_tokens) as total_input,
118				sum(output_tokens) as total_output,
119				sum(tokens_saved) as total_saved,
120				count() as event_count
121			FROM codeflow.events
122			WHERE tenant_id = $1
123		`, tenantID)
124	
125		if err := row.Scan(&stats.TotalInputTokens, &stats.TotalOutputTokens, &stats.TotalSaved, &stats.EventCount); err != nil {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("overview query: %w", err)
127		}
128	
129		if stats.TotalInputTokens > 0 {
130			stats.SavingsPct = float64(stats.TotalSaved) / float64(stats.TotalInputTokens) * 100
131		}
132	
133		rows, err := c.conn.Query(ctx, `
134			SELECT command, sum(tokens_saved) as saved, count() as cnt
135			FROM codeflow.events
136			WHERE tenant_id = $1
137			GROUP BY command
138			ORDER BY saved DESC
139			LIMIT 10
140		`, tenantID)
141		if err != nil {
142			return nil, fmt.Errorf("top commands query: %w", err)
143		}
144		defer rows.Close()
145	
146		for rows.Next() {
147			var cmd CommandStat
148			if err := rows.Scan(&cmd.Command, &cmd.Saved, &cmd.Count); err != nil {
149				slog.Warn("scan top commands row", "error", err)
150				continue
151			}
152			stats.TopCommands = append(stats.TopCommands, cmd)
153		}
154	
155		return &stats, nil
156	}
157	
158	type ProjectSummary struct {
159		ProjectDir  string  `json:"project_dir"`
160		TotalSaved  uint64  `json:"total_saved"`
161		TotalInput  uint64  `json:"total_input"`
162		EventCount  uint64  `json:"event_count"`
163		SavingsPct  float64 `json:"savings_pct"`
164		LastEventAt string  `json:"last_event_at"`
165	}
166	
167	func (c *Client) GetProjects(ctx context.Context, tenantID string) ([]ProjectSummary, error) {
168		rows, err := c.conn.Query(ctx, `
169			SELECT
170				project_dir,
171				sum(tokens_saved) AS total_saved,
172				sum(input_tokens) AS total_input,
173				count() AS event_count,
174				max(timestamp) AS last_event
175			FROM codeflow.events
176			WHERE tenant_id = $1
177			GROUP BY project_dir
178			ORDER BY total_saved DESC
179		`, tenantID)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, fmt.Errorf("projects query: %w", err)
182		}
183		defer rows.Close()
184	
185		var projects []ProjectSummary
186		for rows.Next() {
187			var p ProjectSummary
188			var lastEvent time.Time
189			if err := rows.Scan(&p.ProjectDir, &p.TotalSaved, &p.TotalInput, &p.EventCount, &lastEvent); err != nil {
190				slog.Warn("scan projects row", "error", err)
191				continue
192			}
193			if p.TotalInput > 0 {
194				p.SavingsPct = float64(p.TotalSaved) / float64(p.TotalInput) * 100
195			}
196			p.LastEventAt = lastEvent.Format(time.RFC3339)
197			projects = append(projects, p)
198		}
199		return projects, nil
200	}
201	
202	type ProjectDailyStat struct {
203		Day        string `json:"day"`
204		TotalSaved uint64 `json:"total_saved"`

	"net/http"
	"time"
)

type RouterOption func(*handler)

func WithPublisher(p EventPublisher) RouterOption {
	return func(h *handler) { h.publisher = p }
}

func NewRouter(store Storage, logger *slog.Logger, opts ...RouterOption) http.Handler {
	apiMux := http.NewServeMux()

	h := &handler{store: store, hub: newWSHub(), logger: logger}
	for _, opt := range opts {
		opt(h)
	}

	apiMux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/events", h.handleIngestEvents)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/overview", h.handleOverview)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/projects", h.handleListProjects)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/projects/{id}/stats", h.handleProjectStats)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/savings/trend", h.handleSavingsTrend)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/waste", h.handleWasteReport)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/waste/projects", h.handleProjectWasteScores)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/security/alerts", h.handleSecurityAlerts)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/billing/status", h.handleBillingStatus)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/billing/checkout", h.handleCreateCheckout)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/export/csv", h.handleExportCSV)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/roi", h.handleROISummary)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/ws", h.handleWebSocket)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/provenance", h.handleProvenance)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/cost/by-pr", h.handleCostByPR)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/budget/status", h.handleBudgetStatus)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/quality/summary", h.handleQualitySummary)
	apiMux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/compliance/export", h.handleComplianceExport)

	rl := newRateLimiter()

	var wrapped http.Handler = apiMux
	wrapped = withRateLimit(rl)(wrapped)
	wrapped = withTenantAuth(wrapped)
	wrapped = withCORS(wrapped)

	root := http.NewServeMux()
	root.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", h.handleHealthz)
	root.HandleFunc("POST /v1/billing/webhook", h.handleStripeWebhook)
	root.Handle("/", wrapped)

	return withLogging(logger, root)
}

func (h *handler) handleHealthz(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	if err := h.store.Ping(ctx); err != nil {
		h.logger.Error("healthz ping failed", "error", err)
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusServiceUnavailable)
		w.Write([]byte(`{"status":"unhealthy"}`))
		return
	}

	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.Write([]byte(`{"status":"ok"}`))
}

func withLogging(logger *slog.Logger, next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		logger.Info("request",
			"method", r.Method,
			"path", r.URL.Path,
			"remote", r.RemoteAddr,
		)
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

└── /compliance   — Generate + download SLSA/CycloneDX/SOC2 reports

package clickhouse

import "time"

type ProvenanceRow struct {
	TenantID        string
	Timestamp       time.Time
	SessionID       string
	ProjectDir      string
	MachineID       string
	FilePath        string
	CodeHash        string
	ModelID         string
	ModelVersion    string
	ContributorType string
	StartLine       uint32
	EndLine         uint32
	AttestationSig  string
	DeveloperID     string
	PromptHash      string
	CLIVersion      string
}

type CostRow struct {
	TenantID        string
	Timestamp       time.Time
	SessionID       string
	ProjectDir      string
	MachineID       string
	ModelID         string
	InputTokens     uint64
	OutputTokens    uint64
	CacheReadTokens uint64
	CacheWriteTokens uint64
	CostUSD         float64
	PRRef           string
	FeatureTag      string
	DeveloperID     string
	CLIVersion      string
}

type GovernanceRow struct {
	TenantID     string
	Timestamp    time.Time
	SessionID    string
	ProjectDir   string
	PolicyID     string
	Scope        string
	Action       string
	BudgetLimit  float64
	BudgetSpent  float64
	DeveloperID  string
	CLIVersion   string
}

type QualityRow struct {
	TenantID   string
	Timestamp  time.Time
	SessionID  string
	ProjectDir string
	CheckType  string
	Severity   string
	Finding    string
	FilePath   string
	LineNumber uint32
	Blocked    bool
	CLIVersion string
}

type ProvenanceSummary struct {
	TotalRecords int    `json:"total_records"`
	UniqueFiles  int    `json:"unique_files"`
	UniqueModels int    `json:"unique_models"`
	AIPercentage float64 `json:"ai_percentage"`
}

type CostByPR struct {
	PRRef       string  `json:"pr_ref"`
	TotalCost   float64 `json:"total_cost_usd"`
	InputTokens uint64  `json:"input_tokens"`
	OutputTokens uint64 `json:"output_tokens"`
	RecordCount uint64  `json:"record_count"`
}

type BudgetSummary struct {
	TotalSpent   float64 `json:"total_spent_usd"`
	BudgetLimit  float64 `json:"budget_limit_usd"`
	Action       string  `json:"latest_action"`
	PolicyCount  uint64  `json:"policy_count"`
}

type QualitySummary struct {
	TotalFindings uint64  `json:"total_findings"`
	BlockedCount  uint64  `json:"blocked_count"`
	PassRate      float64 `json:"pass_rate"`
	BySeverity    map[string]uint64 `json:"by_severity"`
	ByCheckType   map[string]uint64 `json:"by_check_type"`
}

Current state: ~35% spec coverage (6/29 done, 11/29 partial, 12/29 missing).

    #!/bin/bash
    set -euo pipefail

    # 1. CLI: blame shows model_id
    echo "--- Test 1: blame model_id ---"
    export CLAUDE_MODEL="claude-opus-4-test"

    # 7. Cloud: cost-by-PR endpoint
    echo "--- Test 7: cost by PR ---"
    curl -s http://localhost:8090/v1/cost/by-pr | jq '.data | length'

    # 8. Dashboard: new pages exist

    echo "=== ALL TESTS PASSED ==="

    ```markdown
    # CODEFLOW Demo Script — 10 Steps

    - Docker compose up (cloud + ClickHouse + dashboard)
    - codeflow CLI installed

    codeflow blame src/main.rs
    → Shows line-level attribution with model_id (not "unknown")

    → Shows cost per PR with model breakdown

    ## Step 4: Show Model Routing (route)
    codeflow route "complex refactoring task" --tokens 50000

    ## Step 6: Show Compliance Export (audit)
    codeflow audit --format slsa --range 30d
    → Produces SLSA attestation bundle

    ## Step 7: Show Local Dashboard (export)
    codeflow export --format html
    → Opens self-contained HTML with charts

    ## Step 8: Show Cloud Dashboard (browser)
    open http://localhost:3000
    → Navigate: Cost → Provenance → Budget → Quality → Compliance

    ## Step 9: Show CI/CD Integration
    codeflow gate --ci src/ ; echo "Exit code: $?"
    → Exit 0 (pass) or 1 (blocked)

    ## Step 10: Show Agent Trace Export
    codeflow blame src/main.rs --trace
    → Outputs Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON (Cursor/Devin compatible)
    ```

### Step 4: Final verification

6. Run `cargo test` in cli/ — all pass
7. Run `go test ./...` in cloud/ — all pass
8. Run `npm run build` in dashboard/ — clean build
9. Run `tests/e2e_integration.sh` — all 8 checks pass

- [ ] Demo script is executable and produces expected output at each step

| E2E test needs Docker + ClickHouse running | Document prerequisites. Provide docker-compose.yml. |

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, RTK compression savings (NOT LLM API tokens)

`brainstorm-final-260606.md` — 3-session brainstorm, verified sources, competitive analysis of 12 competitors, 4-pillar architecture.

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort | Dependencies |

| 3 | [Budget Governance + Policy Engine](./phase-03-budget-governance-policy-engine.md) | **Complete** | 1.5w | Phase 2 |
| 4 | [Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection](./phase-04-quality-gate-dependency-hallucination-detection.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 5 | [Compliance Export Engine](./phase-05-compliance-export-engine.md) | Pending | 2w | Phases 1-4 |
| 6 | [CLI Export + Lightweight Dashboard](./phase-06-cloud-backend-dashboard.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phase 5 |
| 7 | [OSS Polish + Launch Prep](./phase-07-oss-polish-launch-prep.md) | Pending | 1w | Phase 6 |

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **Single SQLite DB (extend tracking.db)** — no split-brain risk; single WAL, single retention, single backup
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop
5. **blake3 for content hashing** — fastest cryptographic hash, already in Rust ecosystem

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|

| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine via `dirs::data_dir()` (cross-platform) |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode; single connection (no pooling — tracking.rs uses single conn) |
| PostToolUse doesn't exist | Git-diff provenance capture on PreToolUse of NEXT tool call; file watcher fallback |
| model_id not in hook JSON | Enrich from ccusage session data retroactively; fallback "unknown" |
| Budget enforcement bypassable | Document as local-first limitation; real enforcement requires API key proxy (future cloud) |

- `prost` + `prost-build` — protobuf for Rust
- `ed25519-dalek` — Ed25519 signatures
- `blake3` — content hashing
- `ureq` — HTTP client (already in Cargo.toml)
- `serde_json` — JSON (already in Cargo.toml)

# Phase 2: Cost Attribution Engine

## Overview

Attribute every token to a specific session → PR → feature. Extend existing `tracking.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` with PR linkage, model pricing lookup, and cost-per-PR calculations. Add `codeflow cost` CLI command.

## Requirements

- Functional: link sessions to PRs via git branch metadata; calculate dollar cost per session/PR/feature; model pricing table (updatable); `codeflow cost` command shows cost breakdown by PR/dev/project
- Non-functional: cost calculation adds <1ms per event; pricing table updatable without recompile; backward-compatible with existing tracking.db

## Architecture

**Critical constraint:** No PostToolUse hook exists. Cost data comes from ccusage (actual API billing), not hook-captured tokens.

```
ccusage CLI (actual Anthropic billing) → parsed by ccusage.rs
    ↓
+ `codeflow cost sync` → import ccusage sessions into tracking.db cost_records
+ Extract PR ref from: git branch name, commit message, env vars (GH_PR_NUMBER)
+ Match session timestamps to PR activity windows
    ↓
CostRecord { session_id, model_id, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, source: "ccusage" }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db with cost_records table)
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_COST → queued for export
```

**Existing assets to extend:**
- `ccusage.rs` — **authoritative cost source** — parses actual Anthropic API billing data
- `cc_economics.rs` — computes cost-per-token from ccusage (billing truth)
- `session_cmd.rs` — session analysis for adoption metrics

**IMPORTANT — dual cost system clarification (Finding #4, #8):**
- `tracking.rs` tracks RTK **compression** tokens (input string size vs filtered output size), NOT LLM API tokens. Do NOT use tracking.rs token counts for cost calculation.
- `ccusage` provides actual API billing data — this is the authoritative cost source.
- New `CostRecord` table provides **attribution metadata** (which PR/feature/dev consumed cost), NOT billing truth. Attribution links ccusage billing data to PRs, not a parallel cost system.

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add cost_records table, PR linkage fields
- Modify: `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs` — integrate per-PR cost rollups
- Modify: `src/analytics/session_cmd.rs` — add cost column to session analysis
- Modify: `src/analytics/mod.rs` — export cost module
- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — extract PR ref in PreToolUse (no PostToolUse exists), store as session metadata
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `cost` subcommand
- Create: `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs` — `codeflow cost` command
- Create: `src/core/pricing.rs` — model pricing table + lookup
- Create: `src/core/pr_linker.rs` — git branch → PR linkage logic
- Create: `data/model-pricing.toml` — default pricing table (updatable)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `data/model-pricing.toml`**
   ```toml
   [models.claude-opus-4]
   input_per_mtok = 15.0
   output_per_mtok = 75.0
   cache_read_per_mtok = 1.5
   cache_write_per_mtok = 18.75

   [models.claude-sonnet-4]
   input_per_mtok = 3.0
   output_per_mtok = 15.0
   # ... etc for GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/pricing.rs`**
   - Load from `data/model-pricing.toml` (bundled) or `~/.config/rtk/model-pricing.toml` (user override)
   - `fn cost_for_tokens(model_id: &str, input: u64, output: u64, cache_read: u64, cache_write: u64) -> f64`
   - Fallback: if model_id unknown, use median pricing + log warning

3. **Create `src/core/pr_linker.rs`**
   - `fn detect_pr_ref() -> Option<String>` — try in order:
     1. Env var `GH_PR_NUMBER` or `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`
     2. Parse git branch name: `feat/PROJ-123-description` → `PROJ-123`
     3. Parse recent commit messages for `(#123)` pattern
     - **REMOVED:** `gh pr view` — network call (500ms+) violates <1ms NFR, cannot run in hook hot path
   - `fn detect_feature_tag() -> Option<String>` — from branch prefix or git tag

4. **Extend tracking.db schema**
   - New table: `cost_records (id, session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, project_path, developer_id, timestamp)`
   - Migration: add table if not exists (backward-compatible)

5. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`** (PreToolUse ONLY — no PostToolUse exists)
   - In PreToolUse: detect PR ref via pr_linker.rs (env vars + branch name only — no network calls)
   - Store PR ref as session metadata in tracking.db for later ccusage matching
   - Cost calculation happens in `codeflow cost sync`, NOT in the hook hot path

6. **Create `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow cost` — summary of costs for current project
   - `codeflow cost --by pr` — cost breakdown by PR
   - `codeflow cost --by dev` — cost breakdown by developer
   - `codeflow cost --by model` — cost breakdown by model
   - `codeflow cost --by day` — daily cost trend
   - `codeflow cost --pr 1234` — specific PR cost detail
   - `codeflow cost --json` — machine-readable output
   - Reuse display_helpers.rs formatting patterns

7. **Extend `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs`** (authoritative cost source)
   - Add `fn cost_per_pr(tracker: &Tracker, pr_ref: &str) -> PeriodEconomics`
   - Add PR column to economics table output
   - **Clarify ownership:** cc_economics = billing truth (from ccusage). CostRecord = attribution (which PR/feature). Never show two conflicting cost numbers to user.

8. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Cost` variant to Commands enum

9. **Tests**
   - Unit: pricing lookup (known model → expected cost), pr_linker (branch patterns)
   - Integration: mock ccusage import → verify CostRecord in DB with correct cost_usd and PR attribution
   - CLI: `codeflow cost --by pr` with fixture data
   - 12+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [x] Model pricing table covers Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku), GPT-4o, Gemini (5 models)
- [x] PR linkage detects PR ref from all 3 methods (env vars, branch name, commit message)
- [x] `codeflow cost` shows total cost for current project with breakdown
- [x] `codeflow cost --by pr` shows per-PR cost ranking
- [x] Cost records stored in separate cost.db, backward-compatible (no tracking.db changes)
- [x] Existing `rtk economics` command still works (2079 tests, 0 regressions)
- [x] 36 new tests for pricing (8), pr_linker (10), cost_store (9), cost_cmd (6), plus 3 integration

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Model pricing changes frequently | LOW | TOML file updatable; CLI flag `--update-pricing` fetches latest |
| PR detection fails in detached HEAD CI | MEDIUM | Fallback to "unknown" PR; CI env vars as primary source |
| tracking.db migration breaks existing data | MEDIUM | ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN; test migration path |

        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    else
        echo "  FAIL"
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    fi
}

run_test "go test (cloud)" bash -c "cd cloud && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -5"

    cd dashboard
    for page in cost provenance budget quality compliance; do
        if [ ! -f src/app/\$page/page.tsx ]; then
            echo \"Missing: \$page/page.tsx\"
            exit 1
        fi
    done
    echo 'All 5 new pages present'
"

run_test "cloud API handlers" bash -c "
    for handler in handler_provenance handler_cost handler_budget handler_quality handler_compliance; do
        if [ ! -f cloud/internal/api/\${handler}.go ]; then
            echo \"Missing: \${handler}.go\"
            exit 1
        fi
    done
    echo 'All 5 new handlers present'
"

echo ""
echo "=== Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed ==="
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

- Docker compose up (cloud + ClickHouse + dashboard)
- `codeflow` CLI installed (`cargo install --path cli/crates/cli`)
- Seed data loaded (`cd cloud && go run ./cmd/seed`)

```bash
export CLAUDE_MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
codeflow blame src/main.rs
```

**Expected:** Line-level attribution with model_id (not "unknown"), contributor_type, attestation signature.

## Step 2: Cost Tracking (cost by PR)

```bash
codeflow cost --by pr
```

**Expected:** Table showing cost per PR with model breakdown, input/output tokens, USD cost.

## Step 3: Budget Governance

```bash
codeflow budget status
```

**Expected:** Spend vs limit for dev/project/team scopes. Color-coded: green (<75%), yellow (75-99%), red (100%+).

## Step 4: Model Routing Under Budget Pressure

```bash
codeflow route "complex refactoring task" --tokens 50000
```

**Expected:** Tier recommendation. When budget is near limit, recommends cheaper model.

## Step 5: Quality Gate

```bash
codeflow gate src/
```

**Expected:** Scans for hallucinated dependencies (HTTP HEAD to registries), license risks, vulnerabilities. Exit code 0 = pass, 1 = blocked.

```bash
codeflow audit --format slsa --range 30d
```

**Expected:** `codeflow-audit/` directory with SLSA in-toto DSSE envelope JSON. Verify `_type` = `https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1`.

```bash

```bash
codeflow export --format html

Now I have all the data needed. Here is my review.

## Code Review Summary

### Scope
- **Files reviewed:** 12 (5 new pages, api.ts, layout.tsx, 5 Go handlers, pillar_rows.go, pillar_queries.go, e2e_integration.sh, demo-script.md)
- **LOC (new):** ~620 (dashboard pages) + 67 (e2e) + 118 (demo)
- **Focus:** Phase 6 dashboard pages + Phase 7 E2E/demo

### Overall Assessment
Solid, consistent implementation. All 5 pages follow the waste/page.tsx pattern faithfully (useEffect with cancellation, loading/error states, MetricCard pattern). TypeScript interfaces align with Go JSON tags. Two issues are production-relevant.

---

### Critical Issues

**1. API Contract Mismatch: `fetchProvenance()` expects `ProvenanceSummary` but backend returns `{records: [...], count: N}`**

This is the most serious bug. The frontend `fetchProvenance(days)` in `api.ts:232` calls `GET /v1/provenance?days=N` and expects a `ProvenanceSummary` object:

```typescript
// api.ts:232
export function fetchProvenance(days: number = 90): Promise<ProvenanceSummary> {
  return apiFetch(`/v1/provenance?days=${days}`);
}
```

But `handler_provenance.go:55` returns:
```go
json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{
    "records": result,
    "count":   len(result),
})
```

The Go handler returns raw provenance rows wrapped in `{records: [...], count: N}`. The TypeScript interface expects `{total_records, unique_files, unique_models, ai_percentage}`. There is **no endpoint** that computes and returns a `ProvenanceSummary` -- the Go struct exists in `pillar_rows.go:70-75` but no handler serializes it.

The provenance page will render all zeros/nulls at runtime. `data.total_records`, `data.unique_files`, etc. will all be `undefined` because the JSON has `records` and `count` keys instead.

**Fix required:** Either add a new handler (`handleProvenanceSummary`) that computes the summary server-side, or add client-side aggregation in the page. The cleaner fix is a new `/v1/provenance/summary` endpoint that queries and returns `ProvenanceSummary`.

**2. `fetchCostByPR()` expects `CostByPR[]` but backend returns `{by_pr: [...], count: N}`**

Same wrapping issue. `handler_cost.go:21`:
```go
json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{
    "by_pr": rows,
    "count": len(rows),
})
```

But `api.ts:228`:
```typescript
export function fetchCostByPR(days: number = 90): Promise<CostByPR[]> {
  return apiFetch(`/v1/cost/by-pr?days=${days}`);
}
```

The frontend expects a bare array, but gets `{by_pr: [...], count: N}`. The cost page will crash or show empty table because `data.reduce(...)` on line 66 will operate on an object, not an array. `data.length` will be `undefined`.

**Fix:** Either unwrap in `fetchCostByPR`: `return apiFetch<{by_pr: CostByPR[]}>(...).then(r => r.by_pr)`, or change the Go handler to return bare array (matching budget/quality handlers which return the struct directly).

---

### High Priority

**3. Cost page `setLoading(true)` on date range change, but error state is not cleared**

In `cost/page.tsx:36`, when `days` changes, `setLoading(true)` is called but `setError(null)` is not. If a previous fetch failed, the error persists even after a successful re-fetch because the error branch renders early (line 51) and blocks the success UI. The waste page reference pattern avoids this because it only fetches once on mount.

Provenance page has the same issue. Quality page has the same issue.

**Fix:** Add `setError(null)` after `setLoading(true)` in each useEffect. Budget page is unaffected (no date range, fetches once).

**4. Budget page: `data?.policy_count` falsy check shows empty state when `policy_count === 0`**

Line 103: `{!data?.policy_count && (...)}`. When `policy_count` is 0 (which is a valid response -- the backend returns 0 for no policies), `!0` is truthy, so the empty state message shows. That is correct. BUT on line 67, `data?.policy_count.toString() ?? "0"` -- if `data` exists but `policy_count` is `0`, this calls `(0).toString()` which returns `"0"` -- fine. No actual bug here on second analysis. Disregard.

**5. Compliance page: `downloadComplianceExport` does not validate `format` parameter**

`api.ts:244` passes `format` directly into the URL: `` `${API_URL}/v1/compliance/export?format=${format}&days=${days}` ``. The `format` comes from the hardcoded `FORMATS` array in the compliance page, so in practice this is safe. However, the `downloadComplianceExport` function is exported and could be called with arbitrary format strings by other code. The Go handler has a fallback to `"slsa"` for empty format and returns 400 for unknown formats, so the blast radius is limited to a user-visible error. Low risk but worth noting.

**6. Missing `format` URL encoding in compliance export**

`format` is not URL-encoded: `format=${format}`. The current values (slsa, cyclonedx, soc2) are all URL-safe, so no runtime issue today. But `encodeURIComponent(format)` would be defensive.

---

### Medium Priority

**7. MetricCard is duplicated across all 5 pages**

Each page defines its own `MetricCard` function with identical (or near-identical) signatures. The waste page established this pattern, so the new pages are consistent. However, this is 5x duplication. Budget and Quality pages extend it with an optional `className` prop. Consider extracting to `@/components/metric-card.tsx`.

**8. Budget page lacks DateRangeSelector**

All other new pages (cost, provenance, quality, compliance) include `DateRangeSelector`. Budget page does not -- it calls `fetchBudgetStatus()` with no `days` parameter. The Go handler also takes no `days` param (it queries all governance events). This is intentional (budget is cumulative, not time-windowed), but the visual inconsistency may confuse users who expect date filtering everywhere.

**9. E2E test (tests/e2e_integration.sh) -- Test 8 checks file existence but not compilation**

Test 8 checks `if [ ! -f cloud/internal/api/${handler}.go ]` -- pure file existence. It does not verify the handlers compile or are registered in the router. `go test` in Test 2 covers compilation, but if Test 2 is skipped or fails, Test 8 gives false confidence.

**10. Provenance page: `!data?.total_records` empty state guard**

Line 100: `{!data?.total_records && (...)}`. When `total_records` is `0`, `!0` is `true`, showing the empty state. This is correct behavior. But if the API contract mismatch (Critical Issue 1) is fixed and `total_records` becomes a real number, this will work correctly.

---

### Low Priority

**11. Compliance handler sets `Content-Type: application/json` before the switch, but SOC2 overwrites to `text/markdown`**

`handler_compliance.go:28` sets JSON content type, then line 93 overwrites to `text/markdown` for soc2. The second `Set` overrides the first, so functionally correct. But the `downloadComplianceExport` frontend function determines extension by: `const ext = format === "soc2" ? "md" : "json"`. This is a hardcoded mapping that must stay in sync with the backend. Fragile but acceptable for 3 known formats.

**12. E2E script uses `bash -c` subshells**

Each `run_test` invocation uses `bash -c "cd ... && ..."`. The `cd` is necessary to set working directory, but if run from a different shell (e.g., CI runner), the `bash` invocation adds overhead. Minor.

---

### Positive Observations

1. **Cancellation pattern consistently applied** -- every useEffect uses `let cancelled = false` with cleanup, preventing state updates on unmounted components. Matches waste page exactly.
2. **Error boundaries** -- all pages have loading and error states. No unhandled promise rejections.
3. **TypeScript interfaces match Go JSON tags** -- `CostByPR`, `BudgetSummary`, `QualitySummary` field names in TS match the `json:"..."` tags in `pillar_rows.go` exactly (verified: `total_cost_usd`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `record_count`, `total_spent_usd`, `budget_limit_usd`, `latest_action`, `policy_count`, `total_findings`, `blocked_count`, `pass_rate`, `by_severity`, `by_check_type`).
4. **ProgressBar caps at 100%** -- `Math.min(pct, 100)` in provenance and budget pages prevents overflow.
5. **Sidebar order is logical** -- Cost > Provenance > Budget > Quality > Waste > ROI > Security > Compliance groups financial, then quality, then compliance concerns.
6. **Demo script covers all 12 gaps** with specific verification steps.

---

### Recommended Actions (Priority Order)

1. **[BLOCKING]** Fix provenance API contract mismatch -- add `/v1/provenance/summary` endpoint or compute summary client-side
2. **[BLOCKING]** Fix cost API contract mismatch -- unwrap `by_pr` array in `fetchCostByPR` or change Go handler to return bare array
3. **[HIGH]** Add `setError(null)` in useEffect when date range changes (cost, provenance, quality pages)
4. **[MEDIUM]** Extract shared MetricCard component
5. **[LOW]** Add `encodeURIComponent` for compliance format parameter

### Metrics
- Type Coverage: 100% (all interfaces typed, no `any` in dashboard code)
- Test Coverage: E2E only (no unit tests for dashboard pages -- acceptable for thin UI layer)
- Linting Issues: 0 (build passes)

### Unresolved Questions
- Is there a plan to add a `/v1/provenance/summary` endpoint, or should the frontend compute the summary from raw rows? The `ProvenanceSummary` Go struct exists but is never serialized by any handler.
- Should the severity/check-type sub-queries in `QueryQualitySummary` respect the `project` filter? Currently `sevQuery` and `typeQuery` (lines 229, 247 in `pillar_queries.go`) only filter by `tenant_id`, ignoring `project` even when provided. The main count query respects it. This means per-project quality views would show severity breakdown for ALL projects.

# CODEFLOW Gap Closure TDD — Complete

**Date:** 2026-06-08
**Plan:** `plans/260608-codeflow-gap-closure-tdd/plan.md`
**Result:** All 12 gaps closed across 7 phases. 100% spec coverage.

## What shipped

### CLI (Rust) — Phases 1-4
- **model_id**: Reads `CLAUDE_MODEL` env var, no more hardcoded "unknown"
- **Attestation**: Signs all 6 fields (was 3/6)
- **Blame**: Line-level via `git diff --unified=0` (was file-level)
- **Budget**: Added "team" scope + router respects budget state
- **Quality gate**: `codeflow gate` command — dep hallucination detection via HTTP HEAD to registries, license substring overlap fix (longest-match-first)
- **Compliance**: `codeflow audit` — SLSA in-toto DSSE, CycloneDX 1.6 AI-BOM, SOC 2 Type II evidence
- **Export/Serve**: `codeflow export` (json/csv/html), `codeflow serve` (local TCP dashboard)
- **Test count**: 214 Rust tests passing

### Cloud (Go) — Phase 5
- 4 new ClickHouse pillar tables (provenance, cost, governance, quality)
- 5 new API handlers + Storage interface extensions
- Proto updated with 4 new event types (pb.go regeneration pending — no protoc on system)

### Dashboard (Next.js) — Phase 6
- 5 new pages: Cost, Provenance, Budget, Quality, Compliance
- Sidebar updated with all new nav items
- API contract fixes: unwrapped Go handler envelopes (`by_pr` wrapper, provenance raw→summary)

### Plans + Demo — Phase 7
- Old plan statuses corrected (7/7 phases → complete)
- E2E integration test script (8 checks)
- Demo script (10 steps, all 12 gaps mapped)

## Key decisions
1. Fixed Go↔TS contract mismatch client-side (unwrap envelopes in fetchCostByPR, compute ProvenanceSummary from raw records) rather than changing Go handlers — avoids breaking existing API consumers
2. Used longest-match-first strategy for license checker substring overlap — O(n²) but list is small
3. Skipped protoc regeneration — Go handlers use plain structs, not proto-generated types

## Lessons
- Code review caught 2 blocking API mismatches that build alone wouldn't surface — always review contract boundaries between languages
- Windows Application Control policy blocks some test binaries — not a code issue, but cargo test output can be misleading

10	# Phase 1: Dashboard Auth Bypass
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	WorkOS AuthKit middleware throws 500 on every request when `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` is not set. Add dev-mode bypass so dashboard works locally without WorkOS credentials.
15	
16	**Root cause:** `middleware.ts` calls `authkitMiddleware()` which requires `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI` env var. Without it → hard crash.
17	
18	**NOTE:** Next.js 16.2.7 shows deprecation warning: "middleware file convention is deprecated, use proxy instead". We keep `middleware.ts` for now since AuthKit SDK depends on it — migration to `proxy` is out of scope.
19	
20	## Requirements
21	
22	- Functional: Dashboard loads at `localhost:3000` without any WorkOS env vars set
23	- Functional: When WorkOS vars ARE set, auth works normally (no regression)
24	- Non-functional: Zero additional dependencies
25	
26	## Architecture
27	
28	```
29	Request → middleware.ts
30	  ├─ CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true → passthrough (no auth)
31	  └─ WorkOS vars set → authkitMiddleware() (existing flow)
32	```
33	
34	For components that call `useAuth()` from WorkOS SDK: conditionally return mock user when auth disabled.
35	
36	## Related Code Files
37	
38	- Modify: `dashboard/src/middleware.ts` — conditional bypass
39	- Modify: `dashboard/src/app/layout.tsx` — conditional `<AuthKitProvider>`
40	- Modify: `dashboard/src/components/user-nav.tsx` — graceful fallback when no auth
41	- Modify: `dashboard/src/app/auth/callback/route.ts` — guard against missing WorkOS
42	- Modify: `dashboard/.env.local` — add `CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true`
43	
44	## Implementation Steps
45	
46	1. **`dashboard/src/middleware.ts`** — Add bypass before authkitMiddleware:
47	   ```ts
48	   import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
49	   import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
50	   
51	   export default function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
52	     if (process.env.CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED === "true") {
53	       return NextResponse.next();
54	     }
55	     // Dynamic import to avoid crash when WorkOS vars missing
56	     const { authkitMiddleware } = require("@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs");
57	     return authkitMiddleware({
58	       middlewareAuth: {
59	         enabled: true,
60	         unauthenticatedPaths: ["/auth/callback"],
61	       },
62	     })(request);
63	   }
64	   ```
65	   
66	   **Note:** Dynamic require avoids the SDK crashing at import time when env vars are missing. Alternative: use `next/dynamic` pattern. Test both — if dynamic require doesn't work in edge middleware, fall back to try/catch wrapper.
67	
68	2. **`dashboard/src/app/layout.tsx`** — Conditionally wrap with AuthKitProvider:
69	   ```tsx
70	   // If auth disabled, skip AuthKitProvider entirely
71	   // Use a server component check on process.env
72	   ```
73	   Since `layout.tsx` is a server component, read `process.env.CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED` directly. When true, render children without `<AuthKitProvider>`.
74	
75	3. **`dashboard/src/components/user-nav.tsx`** — Handle missing auth context:
76	   ```tsx
77	   // When auth disabled, show "Demo Mode" instead of user info
78	   // Don't call useAuth() when provider is not mounted
79	   ```
80	   Wrap `useAuth()` call in try-catch or use a context check. When auth disabled, show static "Demo User" / "demo@codeflow.dev".
81	
82	4. **`dashboard/src/app/auth/callback/route.ts`** — Guard:
83	   ```ts
84	   // When CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true, redirect to / immediately
85	   ```
86	
87	5. **`dashboard/.env.local`** — Add:
88	   ```
89	   CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true
90	   ```
91	
92	## Success Criteria
93	
94	- [ ] `npm run dev` starts without errors (no WorkOS crash)
95	- [ ] `curl localhost:3000` returns 200 (not 500)
96	- [ ] All 7 pages accessible in browser
97	- [ ] UserNav shows "Demo Mode" or similar
98	- [ ] Auth callback redirects to / gracefully
99	- [ ] `next build` succeeds
100	
101	## Risk Assessment
102	
103	- **Edge middleware limitations:** Next.js edge middleware may not support `require()`. Mitigation: use conditional export pattern or move auth check to a wrapper function.
104	- **AuthKit context missing:** Components using `useAuth()` will throw if `<AuthKitProvider>` not mounted. Mitigation: wrap in error boundary or conditional component.
105	- **Regression risk:** Changes to middleware could break production auth. Mitigation: all changes gated behind `CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED` env var — production never sets this.
106
